note: Installation ID, installation timestamp and license survive a restore: the full-cycle test of Task 5 asserts them.

The license state is computed from the clock and never locks for a certificate whose notBefore is ahead (proven). R28's admin warning "system clock appears to be behind" from certificate evidence is not built; the clock_behind banner comes from the time record only.

State, effective time and banners are identical with and without certificates whose notBefore is 3 or 100 years ahead, before and after a restart; no clock event is recorded (the optional warning is not raised).
No test restarts PostgreSQL under a running deployment job. Related evidence: the crash-recovery sweep and lease rules (F-66) and pgxpool's reconnect.
The friendly 503, /healthz failing and /livez passing are proven; that jobs pause and nothing is lost after two minutes without the database is not tested.

The backup file holds no plaintext canary (F-87, test). The release tarball is the two scanned images plus repository files: make secrets-scan (gitleaks, history), fs-scan and image-scan (Trivy, secret scanner) are gates of make ci and make release-gates, recorded in docs/security/reviews/phase-8.md; no test scans the packed tarball itself.

/test/* is absent from the release build; no build links net/http/pprof, expvar or a metrics library, and the release server answers /debug/pprof, /debug/vars and /metrics with no profile, variable or metric data.
Zeroing is proven for request secrets and the OpenSSH key block; no guarantee against the Go GC is claimed.
The 200-sample statistical timing test is deferred; the shape and status equality is proven by the listed test and the equal-work dummy Argon2 verification by internal/auth tests.

Bounded concurrent Argon2, the 5-a-minute backup download and Phase 8 action buckets (audit forwarding test, back up now, HTTPS upload) and the per-target SSH connection bound are proven. A server test connection has only the general per-identity limit and the SSH pool bound; no stricter per-route limit is built for it.

TLS 1.2 minimum (test); the release compose publishes only the HTTPS port (no port 80 listener, test). The testssl.sh grade is the make testssl gate of make release-gates and make nightly (A+ on the release image, docs/security/reviews/phase-8.md); the real host is owner item 4.

note: Script and HTML in certificate common names and labels, server names and addresses, SSH key comments, audit actors, objects and reasons render as text with no element, handler or javascript: link (rendered pages, jsdom); the page CSP is tested. Not done: the in-browser Playwright run with fixtures that checks a marker under the CSP.

Shell injection through every string that reaches the helper or SSH is proven. SQL: every query is parameterized (gosec G201/G202 in make lint, the no-string-building rule) and FuzzOpenAPIInputs fuzzes every create/update body; no test sends SQL-injection payloads through every list, filter and sort parameter, and the active ZAP scan (make zap-full) is an owner/CI gate.
The hardening script (make e2e-hardening-check, run by make ci) checks the running containers; the release compose test checks user, read-only root, capabilities and that PostgreSQL is not published.

Pins and lockfile shape (tests), go mod verify (make vuln); the stage carries the three SBOMs and refuses missing inputs, the release tools sign and the scripts and the release harness refuse a bad or missing signature (tests). The production signature is the owner's ceremony.
